subject: Conversation stall: streaming chat stutter and mitigation
messages:
From: Sarah Chen <sarah@omnify.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: ops@omnify.ai
Date: 2027-04-28T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: Production: streaming chat stutters (tokens arrive in bursts)

Hi Vanessa / Rishi —

We started seeing significant stuttering on our production streaming/chat endpoint around 07:50 PDT. Users report that responses arrive in short bursts (a few tokens), then pause for 1–8+ seconds before the next chunk. Throughput looks normal, but user experience is degraded and a few sessions time out.

What we've observed:
- Region: us-west-2 (primary)
- SDK: omnify-chat-js v2.3.1 (web)
- Endpoint: POST /v1/generate-stream (model: redwood-compat-13B)
- Affected % of sessions: ~18% of active sessions, concentrated on long-context flows (>= 600 tokens)
- Sample user/session IDs attached in omnify-client-logs-0428.txt

We need immediate mitigation guidance and an ETA for a fix. For now we have rolled our web clients to retry logic but hit UX flicker. Any quick configuration changes that we can push from our side?

Please escalate — this is impacting our customer-facing chat.

Thanks,
Sarah Chen
Head of Product, Omnify
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah@omnify.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-28T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: streaming chat stutters (tokens arrive in bursts)

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the details and the logs — filing this with infra now. Immediate guidance we recommend to reduce user-facing impact (quick steps you can push in the next 10–30 minutes):

1) Switch critical flows to non-streaming fallbacks: call the same generation endpoint with stream=false for highest-impact screens. This will increase end-to-end latency by the total generation time but removes chunk pacing artifacts.

2) Temporarily reduce max_tokens to ~512 for long conversations (where feasible) — fewer tokens reduces cache churn and the number of streaming chunks.

3) If you have multi-region routing, route a subset of traffic to a different region (us-east-1) for the next hour to confirm it's region-specific.

4) As a short-term server-side mitigation we can route your production traffic to a non-quantized, lower-latency variant (redwood-lite-13B) for impacted sessions — this reduces the chance of chunking pauses. I can enable that routing for you immediately if you approve.

We've opened INC-2045 and attached an initial capture (redwood-initial-capture-0428.json). Our SREs are triaging; Rishi is on the thread and will provide a triage note in the next update.

I'll keep you posted every 30–60 minutes until we have a fix. If you want we can stand up a quick call now — otherwise I'll proceed with the routing toggle if you authorize it.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, Sarah Chen <sarah@omnify.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-28T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: streaming chat stutters (tokens arrive in bursts)

Quick triage update from infra: we've correlated the pauses with repeated KV-cache evictions on the edge shard group serving Omnify traffic. Observations:

- Memory pressure spikes on shard(s) eu/redundant-130 and us-west-2-edge-21 around 07:45–08:05 PDT.
- Evictions cause repeated re-materialization of prefix state which increases per-token compute and introduces uneven token emission (burst then pause).
- Metrics: stream_chunk_delay_ms spikes from ~25ms baseline to >1200ms at peak; cache_eviction_rate up by 4.3x.

Immediate mitigations we are applying:
- Pinning your routing to non-quantized variants for the affected nodes (reduces re-materialization overhead).
- Increasing prefix-cache TTL for your customer namespace to avoid aggressive eviction.
- Rolling a hotfix to edge autoscaler to better respect persistent-namespace cache reservations (rollout started).

Estimated timeline: hotfix rollout in ~6 hours (global staggered rollout), full root-cause fix (kernel-level allocator change + regression test) targeted within 72 hours.

I've attached server traces and the capture we pulled (inc-2045-server-trace-0428.log). Will update with roll progress in the next 30–60 minutes.

— Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Chen <sarah@omnify.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-28T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: streaming chat stutters (tokens arrive in bursts)

Thanks — we flipped the most sensitive flows to non-streaming and we see the UX is much smoother (no more 5–8s pauses) but it's not ideal for our live chat product. We also approved the routing toggle to redwood-lite-13B and saw an improvement in token pacing.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood provide an ETA for a permanent fix and a short summary we can share with our execs?
2) Given user impact and increased engineering hours on our side, what's the process for a credit/compensation?

Also please put us on a postmortem call — prefer tomorrow morning PT.

— Sarah
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah@omnify.ai>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-29T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Conversation stall — next steps, postmortem invite, and credit

Hi Sarah / Omnify team —

Summary and next steps following yesterday's incident:

What happened
- Between 07:45–08:15 PDT on 2027-04-28 a subset of edge shards experienced elevated memory pressure causing increased KV-cache evictions. Evictions caused repeated re-materialization of prefix state and resulted in uneven token emission for streaming responses (user-observed stuttering).

Immediate mitigations performed
- Temporary routing to a non-quantized model variant for Omnify traffic.
- Increased prefix-cache TTL for your namespace and pinned cache reservations during the rollout window.
- Guidance delivered to Omnify to fall back to non-streaming for critical flows (implemented by your team).

Short-term status
- Hotfix to edge autoscaler deployed as a staggered rollout; monitoring shows metric recovery and a sharp drop in stream_chunk_delay_ms.
- Customer-facing UX improved after routing toggle and non-streaming fallback.

Permanent fix and timeline
- Root cause: allocation/regression in edge memory management interacting with KV cache retention.
- Permanent fix involves a kernel allocator patch + added regression tests for long-context streaming flows. Target ETA: 72 hours for full validation and controlled rollout; we'll provide daily progress notes.

Compensation proposal
- Redwood proposes a 10% credit on your monthly usage for April as good-faith compensation for the user impact and engineering disruption. We'll follow normal billing process to apply the credit if you accept.

Postmortem review
- Proposed meeting: 2027-04-30 10:00 PT — will include infra, SRE, and your product/engineering leads. Join link: https://meet.redwood.com/vanessa/omnify-postmortem-20270430
- Draft incident report attached (redwood-incident-draft.pdf).

Please reply with confirmation for the meeting time and whether you'd like us to proceed with the compensation credit. We're committed to keeping you updated and minimizing repeat occurrences.

Thanks again for your patience — we take this seriously.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
